application_input.portable_text_domain: sender and sms must contain only Unicode scalar values encodable as strict UTF-8

candidate_id_conventions.ordering_tie_break: ascending source character start and end, followed by the field-specific tie rules below; IDs are assigned after semantic deduplication and PN is always last

enumeration_lexical_domain.regex_classes: \b, \d, \s, and \w use ASCII semantics only; Unicode properties and locale are never consulted
enumeration_lexical_domain.case_insensitive_matching: Only ASCII A through Z fold to ASCII a through z; every other Unicode scalar remains unchanged
enumeration_lexical_domain.semantic_text_normalization: Collapse one or more ASCII whitespace scalars U+0009 through U+000D or U+0020 to U+0020, trim the same set at both ends, and apply ASCII-only lowercase for identity
enumeration_lexical_domain.counterparty_value_alphabet: ASCII letters and digits plus the punctuation explicitly present in the versioned extractor patterns; non-ASCII letters never satisfy an ASCII letter class
enumeration_lexical_domain.currency_markers: literal U+20B9 RUPEE SIGN or ASCII-case-insensitive INR and RS
enumeration_lexical_domain.unicode_dependency: Candidate enumeration has no Unicode database, locale, Java ICU, Swift Foundation, or Python casefold dependency

amount.source_enumeration: Parse canonical decimal_text directly from each currency source token and deduplicate by exact Decimal numeric equality before any binary floating-point projection.
amount.numeric_token_boundary: The complete grouped or ungrouped numeric token is consumed; fractional precision is unbounded and a match is rejected rather than stopped before a following digit, decimal point, or grouping comma.
amount.tie_break: decimal numeric value, decimal_text, then source_text

exact_metadata.decimal_text: finite positive base-10 value with source precision preserved and grouping separators removed
exact_metadata.minor_units: integer paise only when source precision is at most two decimal places and the result is within signed Int64 0 through 9223372036854775807; otherwise null
exact_metadata.app_amount: legacy finite floating-point projection only; decimal_text and minor_units remain authoritative for persistence

account.tie_break: ASCII-lowercased normalized value, normalized value, then source_text

counterparty.tie_break: prefix rank, prefix text, ASCII-lowercased normalized value, normalized value, then source_text

candidate_id_conventions.validation: Every non-PN ID must resolve to exactly one candidate whose normalized value is derived from its validated source_text span in the current SMS; unknown, duplicate, malformed, forged-value, or cross-message IDs fail closed.
candidate_id_conventions.caller_supplied_candidate_sets: A supplied CandidateSet is accepted only when it is exactly equal, including tuple order, contiguous IDs, values, source_text, spans, type hints, and PN-last placement, to deterministic enumeration of the same SMS.

candidate_source_evidence.coordinate_space: UTF-8 bytes of the exact application_input.sms with no Unicode normalization
candidate_source_evidence.source_text_validation: The declared UTF-8 byte slice must decode exactly to source_text, and the candidate value must equal the field-specific normalization of that source_text.

supervision_oracle.accepted_label_forms: null, an exact four-field mapping, lowercase JSON null, or exact JSON text containing the four-field object
supervision_oracle.exact_amount_inputs: Direct mapping integers and Decimal values are compared without binary floating-point conversion; fractional numeric lexemes in exact JSON text are decoded with Decimal-preserving number parsing
supervision_oracle.binary_float_inputs: A finite positive binary float may be used only when exactly one candidate has the same finite binary-float projection

model_output.all_other_unicode_whitespace: not JSON whitespace; before the object is invalid_json and after the object is trailing_content

canonical_serialization.member_order_source: document-specific member_order declarations; selector target order comes from model_output.schemas.*.member_order

string_escaping.other_U+0000_through_U+001F: six ASCII characters \u00xx using lowercase hexadecimal digits
string_escaping.all_other_unicode_scalars: literal UTF-8 with no normalization or optional escaping

canonical_serialization.unicode_normalization: none; preserve source code points so candidate offsets remain valid
canonical_serialization.numbers: base-10 JSON integers without exponent notation; booleans, NaN, and infinity are rejected

hashing.input: the exact canonical UTF-8 bytes with no BOM or trailing newline

candidate_payload.candidate_map_member_order: candidate ID order emitted by deterministic source-span enumeration

model_messages.system_content:
Classify one Indian financial SMS using only the candidates supplied by the user.
Return exactly one compact JSON object and no prose or markdown.
For everything other than a posted bank/card transaction return {"transaction":0}.
For a posted transaction return keys in this exact order: transaction=1, type D or C, amount ID, account ID, counterparty ID.
Counterparty ID PN explicitly means that the SMS contains no counterparty.
Never invent, copy, or modify a value. Select only IDs supplied for this SMS.

model_runtime_defaults.determinism_note: Greedy temperature-zero decoding is required; backend-specific kernels can still require parity verification.

outcomes.rejected_result: No transaction is emitted or persisted. Rejection remains diagnostically distinct from an accepted not-transaction decision.

known_gaps: PocketFinancer Android current has no CandidateProtocolV1 request builder or strict parser.
No iOS source tree or iOS runtime profile is present or validated.
Host reference execution does not establish llama.cpp JNI token or byte parity.
Phone latency, memory, prefilter parity, and end-to-end persistence require an instrumented device run.
platform_parity.claim_policy: Host golden-vector conformance is protocol evidence only and must not be presented as Android runtime or device parity.
